title: Linear relationships
summary: The Cartesian plane, tables and rules, solving equations and inequalities with graphs, intercepts, gradient, y = mx + c, applications and non-linear graphs.

cards.title: The Cartesian plane
cards.rule: \((x, y)\): across first, then up or down. The origin is \((0, 0)\).
lines: \((-2, 3)\) is 2 left and 3 up, in the second quadrant

cards.title: Rules, tables and graphs
cards.rule: Use the rule to fill a table, plot the points and join them.

cards.title: Finding the rule
cards.rule: The step in \(y\) is the number in front of \(x\). The value at \(x = 0\) is the constant.

cards.title: Solving equations with graphs
cards.rule: Read across from the value you want to the line, then down to the x-axis.

cards.title: Solving inequalities with graphs
cards.rule: Find the part of the line above or below the value you want.

cards.title: Gradient
cards.rule: Gradient \(= \dfrac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}\). Up to the right is positive, down is negative.
lines: Horizontal lines have a gradient of 0

cards.title: Gradient–intercept form
cards.rule: \(y = mx + c\): \(m\) is the gradient, \(c\) is the y-intercept.

cards.title: Applications of straight lines
cards.rule: \(c\) is the starting value, \(m\) is the rate.

cards.title: Non-linear graphs
cards.rule: Not every rule gives a straight line. \(y = x^2\) is a parabola.
